evidence: Quint. 1.7.3: eadem littera nōminātīvō cāsū brevis, ablātīvō longa est
Quint. 9.4.86: a brevis, gre brevis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To shorten a vowel or syllable is corripere (Quint. 1.5.18), and a shortened syllable correpta; to pronounce a vowel short, correptē prōnūntiāre (Traupman 248; correptē dīcere, Gell. 2.17.5). A short mark is nota brevis (Traupman 247).

evidence: Quint. 1.5.18: sīve cum syllaba correpta prōdūcitur

phrases.latin: palus aliud priōre syllabā longā aliud sequentī significat
phrases.english: palus means one thing with the first syllable long, another with the second

sources: Lewis & Short: brevis · Lewis & Short: corripio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 247, 248.
